title: Python Output Fundamentals

learningObjectives.description: Use Python's print() function to display text.

conceptExplanations: Python is a programming language: a way to give a computer instructions. A Python interpreter normally reads and executes those instructions.

The print() function displays its argument as text. A string literal is text surrounded by matching single or double quotation marks. The quotation marks are part of the code, not the displayed message.

This pilot does not execute Python. Its restricted text checker recognizes one print call containing one plain, single-line string. It compares the extracted message with the task's expected output, including a final newline.

examples.explanation: print is the function name; parentheses surround the argument; matching quotes mark the string. print normally ends its output with a newline.

audienceAdaptations.title: Introduction to Python: Your First Program

practiceTasks.instruction: Write one print call that displays Hello, Code Coven!
Write one print call that displays Welcome to Code Coven!

successCriteria: Use one lowercase print function call.
Supply one plain string in matching quotes and parentheses.
Match the requested text exactly, including case and punctuation.
evaluationCriteria: Reject unsupported syntax without executing it.
Accept single or double quotes and surrounding horizontal whitespace.
Infer one final newline; do not claim that Python ran.

errorFeedback.empty: Start with print, add parentheses, and place your message inside matching quotes.
errorFeedback.unsupported-syntax: Use exactly one print call with one plain string in matching quotes. This small checker does not support variables, escapes, comments, extra statements, or other Python features.
errorFeedback.output-mismatch: The print pattern is recognized, but the message differs. Compare capitalization, punctuation, spaces, and spelling with the exact expected output.
errorFeedback.too-long: Keep this small practice answer to 500 characters or fewer.
errorFeedback.correct: The text matches this task's expected print pattern. Python was not executed.

safety.performanceClaim: Passing demonstrates successful task performance under this restricted checker, not humanlike understanding, consciousness, or permanent learning.
